spec.name: Trend v18
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.2, annual return 5%, maximum drawdown 8%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.19 to 1.14 (change -0.05).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.19 to 1.19. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.08 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.19); it breaks even at 63.0 bps with daily turnover 0.03.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.19 against 1.19 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -0.08 against 1.19 in research, a gap of +1.27.
The best year gives 31% of total P&L (year 3) and calm regimes give 138%; Sharpe is 2.47 in calm and -1.21 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 270 distinct specs; the best of 270 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.82, so the claimed 1.20 becomes 0.38 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 86%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.29 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.58).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.19 to as low as 0.47 (as low as 0.47 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (22 days) give 49% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 31% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
